# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

The International Trade Administration’s National Travel and Tourism Office (NTTO) has updated its U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor, a data visualization tool highlighting overseas visitation to U.S. states and cities through interactive tables and maps, to calendar year 2024. Highlights for 2024 include:
*   Top state visited by overseas visitors: New York (9,802,000)  
*   Top city-MSA visited by overseas visitors: New York City (9,525,000)  
*   Biggest state # gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Florida (+927,000)  
*   Biggest % gain of overseas visitors from 2023: Vermont (+87.8%)  
*   Top 5 states’ combined market share: 62.0% of overseas visitors  
*   Top 5 city-MSA’s combined market share: 48.5% of overseas visitors
**U.S. States and Cities Visited Monitor** has six sections:
*   **Top 5 States and U.S. Cities in 2024**: volume, gains and declines  
*   **Select a U.S. State**: state rank, volume, # change, % change, market share and top cities-MSAs  
*   **Map of Top States-Cities-MSAs**: interactive display of top cities-MSAs visited in each state  
*   **Top U.S. States Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share  
*   **Top U.S. Cities-MSAs Visited**: table of 2024 rank, market share, # change, % change and 2024 visitation and market share  
*   **Download Data**: download data into excel

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.

New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).

**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.

Last updated September 21, 2026·Originally published September 11, 2024
Let’s clear something up before we go a single step further. **New Jersey has zero of the 64 official national parks.** Not Yellowstone, not Yosemite, not one. If a list promises you “national parks” in the Garden State, it is selling you something that does not exist.
What New Jersey does have is **11 National Park Service experiences** worth your time. Scenic trails, recreation areas, a national monument, a national reserve, a couple of wild rivers, and some of the finest Revolutionary War and industrial history sites in the country. They just carry different designations than “national park.” I am going to walk through all 11 and tell you exactly what each one actually is.
I’m a native New Yorker who has spent plenty of time next door in New Jersey, and since I retired from teaching history in 2018 I’ve made it a point to visit these places in person. I spent a career teaching the history behind these sites. Then I got to stand on the ground where it happened. That is the lens I’m writing from here.
A view of the New Jersey Performing Arts Center building in Newark from the Newark Club. (Courtesy of Wikimedia Commons)
If you’re planning a trip, one book I recommend is **New Jersey Off the Beaten Path: A Guide To Unique Places** by Bill Scheller and Kay Scheller.

Now, let’s get started.
* * *

## #New Jersey NPS Sites At A Glance
Here are all 11 sites, grouped by their correct designation, so you can see at a glance what kind of place each one really is and what you’d go there for.
| Site | NPS Designation | What You Go For |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Appalachian National Scenic Trail | National Scenic Trail | Long-distance hiking, ridgeline views |  
| Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route | National Historic Trail | Driving and walking the 1781 march to Yorktown |  
| Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area | National Recreation Area | Hiking, paddling, camping along the Delaware |  
| Gateway National Recreation Area | National Recreation Area | Beaches, birding, history at Sandy Hook |  
| Statue of Liberty National Monument (Ellis Island) | National Monument | Immigration history and harbor views |  
| Morristown National Historical Park | National Historical Park | Washington’s winter encampments |  
| Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park | National Historical Park | America’s first planned industrial city |  
| Thomas Edison National Historical Park | National Historical Park | Edison’s lab and Glenmont estate |  
| Great Egg Harbor River | National Scenic and Recreational River | Paddling a 129-mile river system |  
| Lower Delaware River | National Wild and Scenic River | Fishing, paddling, river history |  
| New Jersey Pinelands National Reserve | National Reserve (state-managed, NPS-coordinated) | Pine barrens ecology, paddling, solitude |
* * *

## #New Jersey NPS Sites At A Glance
### #1. Appalachian National Scenic Trail
**Designation:** National Scenic Trail (administered by the National Park Service).
The Appalachian Trail (AT) runs 2,190 miles from Springer Mountain in Georgia to Mount Katahdin in Maine, and roughly 72 of those miles cross New Jersey. It was first conceptualized by **Benton MacKaye** in 1921 and completed in 1937 after more than a decade of work by volunteers and the Civilian Conservation Corps.
It was designated the first National Scenic Trail under the National Trails System Act of 1968. The New Jersey stretch is known for boardwalks across wetlands, the bear-heavy ridgeline around High Point and Stokes State Forest, and a steady cast of black bears, deer, and migrating raptors. The Appalachian Trail Conservancy, founded in 1925, still helps maintain and protect it.
What you go for: long-distance hiking and section hiking, ridgeline views, camping at designated sites and shelters, wildlife watching, and trout fishing in the streams the trail crosses.
Appalachian Trail | Courtesy of NPS
* * *

## #Planning Your New Jersey Trip
### #Fees and Logistics
Most of these sites are free to enter, including Morristown, Paterson Great Falls, and the river units. Thomas Edison charges $15 for adults 16 and older, and children 15 and under are free. Sandy Hook at Gateway charges a seasonal beach parking fee in summer. Ellis Island has no entry fee, but the ferry ticket is required and should be reserved ahead in peak season. Always check the official NPS page for each site before you go, since hours and seasonal closures change. An America the Beautiful annual pass does not cover the beach parking fee at Sandy Hook or the amenity fees at Delaware Water Gap, though Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off both.
* * *

## #Check Out Our Acadia National Park Film
* * *
ACADIA National Park 4K (4 Minute Tour)
MTJP | Acadia is the culmination of several weeks spent exploring Acadia National Park during peak fall color. The film is, in part, a celebration of Acadia’s centennial. It is dedicated to George Dorr.
Sculpted by glaciers and landscaped by beavers, Acadia is full of unique features. Rounded mountains, quiet ponds, rocky coastline, and some of the finest trails in the country make up this place.
The film was shot entirely in 4K. Acadia sits on Mt. Desert Island and the Schoodic Peninsula of Maine. Will and Jim chose to film in autumn for its reputation as one of the best places in the world to see fall foliage, and what they captured did not disappoint.
Acadia is a quieter national park with one of the finest road systems in the system, and it holds the first point in the United States the sun touches each morning. Locations Will and Jim captured include Jordan Pond, Bass Harbor Head Lighthouse, Otter Cliffs, Cadillac Mountain, the beaver ponds, and the Schoodic Peninsula.
* * *
**Does New Jersey have any national parks?**
No. None of the 64 official US national parks are in New Jersey. What the state has instead is 11 National Park Service sites and related units, each with its own designation: the Appalachian National Scenic Trail, Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, Ellis Island (part of Statue of Liberty National Monument), Gateway National Recreation Area, Great Egg Harbor River, the Lower Delaware National Wild and Scenic River, Morristown National Historical Park, the New Jersey Pinelands National Reserve, Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park, Thomas Edison National Historical Park, and the Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route National Historic Trail.

You should probably know that this guide does not come out of thin air. More Than Just Parks is a family operation. My sons Will and Jim have spent their entire adult lives exploring America’s national parks and public lands destinations. I taught American history for 25 years, and I write our history and travel guides.
Will and Jim have worked with the National Park Service, the Department of the Interior, the USDA, and the U.S. Forest Service for years. Their work has been featured in leading publications around the world.

# NTTO Releases International Travel Statistics for 2023
## **International Visitor Arrivals to the United States in 2023**
Total international visitor arrivals 1 of 66.5 million in 2023 increased 15.7 million (+31%) from 50.8 million in 2022 to a level 84% of the 79.4 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s ADIS/I-94 Visitor Arrivals program page or can be downloaded here.
NTTO’s latest forecast expects international visitor arrivals to surpass pre-pandemic 2019 levels in 2025 with 85.2 million.
**Major Characteristics of Overseas Visitors to the United States from the Survey of International Air Travelers (SIAT)**
New York was the most-visited state by overseas travelers in 2023, up from #2 in 2022, followed by Florida and California.
New York City was the most-visited city by overseas travelers in 2023, followed by Miami and Los Angeles.
2023 overseas visitation to the following U.S. states/territories surpassed visitation in 2019: Puerto Rico (+85%), Tennessee (+15%), Texas (+7%) and Georgia (+5%).
These and other characteristics of international visitors to the United States can be analyzed in reports on the SIAT Results Inbound page or can be viewed in the SIAT Inbound Survey Monitor data visualization tool.
**U.S. Citizen Departures from the United States in 2023**
Total U.S. citizen departures 2 of 98.5 million in 2023 increased 17.6 million (+22%) from 80.8 million in 2022 to a level 99% of the 99.7 million arrivals in 2019.
Annual international arrivals from 2000 to 2023 covering all countries and world regions are available on NTTO’s APIS/I-92 Visitor Departures Program page or can be directly downloaded here.
